label: Local News
info: Local news stories that you canuse either as a Case or Rumor.

entries.result:
ENERGY ANOMALY
	Utility crews responded to an incident at the Vintage Arcade after a series of transformer blowouts reportedly fried the circuit boards of six arcade machines at once, knocking out the lights and startling customers. Residents nearby also reported strange flick- ering streetlights and televi- sion interference around the same time. Authorities are treating the incident as van- dalism.

UNEXPLAINED SCARS
	St. Luke Memorial Hospital alerted authorities after staff noticed a strange pattern among three patients admitted with minor injuries. Each bore an identical surgical scar at the base of the skull from what appeared to be a recent proce- dure, yet none could remember ever having it done. Hospital officials deny any wrongdoing.

WHO LEFT SANTA?
	Several residents have report- ed finding a life-size Santa Claus statue on their front porches. Those who hauled the heavy decoration inside woke up to find valuables missing, along with the statue itself. Authorities are investigating the incidents.

INVISIBLE VIOLINIST
	For the sixth night in a row, violin playing has been heard drifting through town after midnight. Residents say the melody seems to shift from street to street, even though no musician has been seen. Au- thorities have confirmed that the reports follow a consistent pattern in timing and location, though no source has been identified. Olivia Fletcher de- nies any connection to the performances.

UNMAPPED TRAIL
	A game trail unknown to local hunters was discovered re- cently. The path appears well- traveled yet is absent from any survey records. Those who follow it report arriving at dif- ferent destinations each time, with no consistent or recog- nizable return route. Some hikers also reported finding small handmade charms along the trail, though accounts re- main inconsistent.

MYSTERIOUS MONOLITH
	Residents arriving downtown early this morning discovered a smooth metal monolith standing in the middle of the Main Square. The object mea- sures approximately ten feet tall and bears no seams, mark- ings, or signs of installation. Public Works officials say no permits were issued for the structure. Authorities have cordoned off the area while the investigation continues.

MISSING MACHINERY
	Authorities have sealed off a logging camp after workers reported all heavy equipment had disappeared. The camp was established within a form- er protected forest area that has been closed since the 1970s. Environmental activists led by Luna Harper are con- sidered the primary suspects in what investigators describe as a possible act of sabotage. Authorities say the investi- gation remains ongoing.

LOT 14 MYSTERY
	Trailer park manager Edward Edwards contacted authorities Tuesday morning after receiv- ing repeated complaints about a foul odor coming from Lot 14. Edwards initially blamed the smell on a problem with the park’s septic system, but when he entered the trailer to inves- tigate, he found the interior ransacked, with bloodstains that appeared to have been hastily cleaned.
	The trailer had been rented two weeks earlier to a traveling salesman who identified him- self only as “Thomas”, and who has not been seen since. Wit- nesses reported seeing him speaking with Roadhouse Pub bartender Yelena Voronova shortly before his disappear- ance. Voronova has since been reported missing, and authori- ties have not commented on whether the cases are connect- ed.

BANK SECURITY CHANGE
	The bank’s security contractor has dismissed its entire staff of employees. They have been replaced by men who share the same surname and bear faces that witnesses describe as strikingly similar. Reginald Caldwell declined to comment, and the company also refused to release any contractual information about the new personnel.

CEMETERY INCIDENT
	Gravediggers reported discov- ering several mausoleums that had remained sealed for more than a century now open. The locks remain intact, with no signs of forced entry, and the coffins appear undisturbed. Cemetery officials say the keys have never left the cemetery administration’s custody. Fam- ilies are demanding answers, and officials have declined to comment while authorities investigate.

RED MIST
	Authorities have closed access to the road leading to the abandoned typewriter factory after a dense reddish fog was reported within its perimeter. Witnesses described the fog as carrying a strong odor of sul- fur and iron, and said that any animal entering the area re- portedly returned minutes later in a state of extreme panic. Access to the site re- mains restricted.
